title: Example: Compiler design (lexer + parser)
description: Shows how compiler-design labs are tested: the program reads source text on stdin and prints tokens / parse decisions in a fixed format. See docs/COMPILER_DESIGN.md.

questions.name: Lexical analyzer
questions.description: Read a program from stdin and print every token on its own line as '<CLASS> <lexeme>'. Classes: KEYWORD (int float char if else while for return), IDENTIFIER ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*), NUMBER ([0-9]+), OPERATOR (+ - * / = < > ! and the two-character ==, <=, >=, !=), SYMBOL (; , ( ) { }), UNKNOWN (any other single character). Whitespace separates tokens and is not printed.

static_checks.description: Compares words against a keyword list (strcmp or a keyword table)

test_cases.expected_output:
KEYWORD int
IDENTIFIER x
OPERATOR =
NUMBER 42
SYMBOL ;

KEYWORD if
SYMBOL (
IDENTIFIER a
OPERATOR >=
NUMBER 10
SYMBOL )
SYMBOL {
IDENTIFIER b
OPERATOR =
IDENTIFIER a
OPERATOR +
NUMBER 1
SYMBOL ;
SYMBOL }
KEYWORD else
SYMBOL {
IDENTIFIER b
OPERATOR =
NUMBER 0
SYMBOL ;
SYMBOL }

test_cases.input_data:
while (i != n) i = i * 2;
return i;
test_cases.expected_output:
KEYWORD while
SYMBOL (
IDENTIFIER i
OPERATOR !=
IDENTIFIER n
SYMBOL )
IDENTIFIER i
OPERATOR =
IDENTIFIER i
OPERATOR *
NUMBER 2
SYMBOL ;
KEYWORD return
IDENTIFIER i
SYMBOL ;

questions.name: Recursive-descent parser
questions.description: Recursive-descent parser for E -> T E', E' -> + T E' | e, T -> F T', T' -> * F T' | e, F -> ( E ) | id (id = an identifier). Input: N, then N expressions, one per line (spaces allowed). Print 'Accepted' or 'Rejected' for each line.

static_checks.description: Has a function for E and for T (or similar)
